research.title: Entropy-Based Feature Engineering for Heart-Disease Prediction
research.focus: Information-theoretic feature selection for clinical classifiers
research.detail: Ranks and constructs features by entropy and mutual information so the model keeps the signal that drives generalization and discards what it would otherwise memorize — the methodological backbone of the stacked-ensemble classifier.
research.outcome: Shipped as the Heart-Disease Stacking Ensemble (89.13% CV accuracy)

research.title: Huffman-Inspired Adaptive Data Structures
research.focus: Frequency-weighted structures that shorten the hot path
research.detail: Adapts Huffman's frequency-coding principle to self-adjusting structures so the most-accessed elements sit on the cheapest access path — algorithmic groundwork for low-latency retrieval and indexing.
research.outcome: Informs the ~45 ms retrieval design in the RAG system

research.title: Explainable Retrieval-Based QA Systems
research.focus: Auditable answers with first-class source attribution
research.detail: Hybrid sparse + dense retrieval with linear score fusion and grounded generation, designed so every answer carries the evidence it was built from — an exploration that became a deployed system.
research.outcome: Shipped as the Explainable RAG QA system (α = 0.65, MRR 0.84)

projects.name: Resume Intelligence Platform

NLP pipeline: extract → NER → taxonomy match → parse → score

projects.name: AI Tutor
projects.what: Child-safe AI tutor for Maths, Science & English — in production at AKademy38
projects.detail: A production tutor that answers student doubts across Maths, Science, and English for Years 3, 5, 7, 8 and the GATE cohort, aligned to the SCSA Western Australian curriculum — from a single backend serving web, mobile, and WhatsApp. No RAG: the model answers from its own knowledge, steered by year-level-aware prompt engineering, and every message passes a three-layer safety screen — input moderation → prompt-level rules → output moderation — before it reaches a child. Responses adapt vocabulary, depth, and tone to each year level (Year 3 ~8yo through Year 8 ~14yo, with extension challenges for GATE), admit uncertainty with full worked steps instead of fabricating, and route harm signals to a defined human safeguarding pathway.

evidence.label: defence-in-depth child safety — input moderation → prompt rules → output moderation on every message
age-adaptive responses for Years 3, 5, 7, 8 and the GATE (Gifted & Talented) cohort

projects.name: Booklet Engine
projects.what: Structured AI pipeline for automated educational content — AKademy38
projects.detail: Replaced AKademy38's manual, hand-run AI booklet workflow with a structured generation pipeline: templated prompts, staged generation, and reuse of shared context so each booklet is assembled deterministically instead of re-prompted from scratch. The outcome is consistent output at a fraction of the cost, built to scale across the content catalog.

evidence.label: lower token usage per booklet — ≈40% → ≈4% of the prior per-booklet token budget
of the booklet workflow moved from manual to an automated pipeline — consistent at scale

projects.name: Explainable RAG QA
projects.what: Hybrid retrieval question-answering with source attribution
projects.detail: Routes every query through two retrievers in parallel — BM25 for exact keywords, dense sentence-transformer vectors over ChromaDB for meaning — then fuses scores linearly before a Groq LLM writes a grounded, cited answer.

evidence.label: fusion weight that maximized Mean Reciprocal Rank (0.84) in a 0→1 sweep
retrieval latency at scale, with incremental indexing (no full rebuilds)

projects.name: Heart-Disease Stacking Ensemble
projects.what: A diagnostic classifier that generalizes instead of memorizing
projects.detail: Level-0 Random Forest, XGBoost, and logistic regression feed their probabilities to a level-1 logistic-regression meta-learner — stacked generalization with 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the UCI heart-disease dataset, served over FastAPI.

evidence.label: cross-validated accuracy — 2.4 points over the best single model
